tema: Review of the clinical features, aetiopathogenesis and treatment of fibromyalgia from the biopsychosocial model.
diseno: Critical narrative review of research, guidelines and clinical experience.
hallazgos: Describes successive diagnostic criteria and the hypothesis of an ascending (periphery to CNS) and descending origin of pain; functional neuroimaging shows changes in nociceptive processing and stress-induced sensitization.
conclusion: Multimodal, individualized treatment is required, with a central role for non-pharmacological interventions and shared goals; RCTs with averages can be misleading because of the existence of subgroups.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract (opening text) and conclusions are consistent; the focus is fibromyalgia, with fatigue as an associated symptom, not ME/CFS.

tema: Determines whether people with fibromyalgia have lower hippocampal volume than healthy controls.
diseno: T1 structural MRI in 40 women with fibromyalgia and 22 controls; hippocampal volume with FreeSurfer and ANCOVA controlling for age, brain size, signal quality and depression (BDI).
hallazgos: The hippocampi were significantly smaller in both hemispheres (left P = 0.037; right P = 0.019), with no significant effect of depression.
conclusion: The hippocampal reduction is not explained by age, disease duration, brain size or depression, and could be related to cognitive complaints; further research is warranted.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on hippocampal volume, memory and depression; the mechanisms of excitotoxicity and glucocorticoids are only proposed in the abstract. A study in fibromyalgia, not in ME/CFS.

tema: Reviews the mechanisms of post-COVID syndrome (PCS) and ME/CFS and proposes a strategy to develop curative therapies.
diseno: Narrative review with a clinical trial platform proposal; provides no own data.
hallazgos: Potential mechanisms identified are immune dysregulation, autoimmunity, endothelial dysfunction, viral persistence and reactivation, with biomarker heterogeneity and overlap with post-infectious ME/CFS. No curative therapies are available.
conclusion: They propose clinical trial networks that evaluate drugs targeting different mechanisms with harmonized diagnostic and outcome criteria and subgroups defined by clinical and biomarker phenotyping.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the keywords reproduce the mechanisms of the abstract. The PDF conclusions are brief and reaffirm the multimodal platform, with a table fragment of drugs with no content.

tema: Evaluates the extent to which PEM is addressed in Norwegian specialist ME/CFS care and its effect on outcomes and quality of care.
diseno: Two cross-sectional online surveys: 788 rehabilitation stays, 86 consultations and 89 hospital interventions; logistic regression, Mann-Whitney U, Spearman correlation and Cronbach's alpha.
hallazgos: PEM was not addressed in more than half of consultations and stays and in a third of interventions; not addressing it doubled the probability of deterioration; a focus on PEM was associated with greater satisfaction, benefit and perceived professional knowledge (α ≥ 0.80).
conclusion: Ignoring PEM makes care ineffective, harmful and of low quality; it is essential to raise awareness among professionals about ME/CFS and PEM, with probable relevance for long COVID.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are more forceful than the abstract (they describe the care as harmful) and provide the proportions of non-addressing.

tema: Reviews the relationship between human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) and the development of autoimmune diseases.
diseno: Narrative literature review of endocrine, neurological and connective tissue autoimmune diseases linked to HHV-6.
hallazgos: HHV-6 has broad cellular tropism, capacity for latency, reactivation and persistence, and multiple immunomodulation tactics; it is frequently found in affected tissues (e.g., multiple sclerosis, autoimmune thyroiditis). Mechanisms such as molecular mimicry and viral persistence have been demonstrated for it.
conclusion: HHV-6 is a candidate trigger of autoimmunity, but more research is needed in tissues, on viral proteins (such as GPCR-type chemokine receptors) and with better methodology (viral species, proteomics, chromosomally integrated HHV-6).
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on viral autoimmunity. The PDF conclusions add methodological limitations and the connection with autoantibodies against GPCRs; ME/CFS does not appear explicitly in any of the sources.

tema: Compares oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) capacity and muscle mitochondrial morphology in CFS, post-COVID syndrome (PCS) and healthy controls.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with muscle biopsies: high-resolution respirometry in permeabilized fibres and electron microscopy (shape, cristae, diameter, area, content). Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Complex I OXPHOS capacity was reduced in PCS versus controls. In subsarcolemmal mitochondria, area, volume, diameter and perimeter were greater in PCS than in CFS, and cristae integrity was greater in PCS, indicating more advanced morphological alterations in CFS.
conclusion: Both groups show altered mitochondrial function; in CFS the structural changes suggest adaptation to prolonged inactivity or unknown molecular causes (e.g., ROS), and in PCS the complex I deficit suggests a direct viral effect and a possible therapeutic target.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add nuances: they acknowledge that the lower OXPHOS in PCS could be due to inactivity and propose complex I as a target, an aspect not present in the abstract.

tema: Groups candidate genes into biological factors and analyses their association with ME/CFS, fibromyalgia and depression.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with leukocyte mRNA expression in 261 people: 61 controls, 15 with fibromyalgia, 33 with ME/CFS, 79 with both and 73 with depression (resistant or medication-responsive); exploratory factor analysis of 34 candidate genes and regression.
hallazgos: 4 factors emerged that explained 51% of the variance: purinergic and cellular modulators, neuronal growth and immunity, nociception and stress mediators, and energy and mitochondrial function. Factors 1 and 3 were positively associated with ME/CFS and negatively with depression severity, with no relationship to fibromyalgia.
conclusion: Candidate gene expression groups into biologically meaningful clusters, and ME/CFS and depression are associated with the same factors in opposite directions; factor analysis could help define subgroups.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on gene expression, purinergic signalling and the comparison with fibromyalgia and depression. The conclusions describe the results as preliminary, call for a longitudinal confirmatory analysis and argue for studying these populations as combinations of diseases.

tema: Analyses mRNA expression of sensory, adrenergic and immune genes in leukocytes of patients with CFS and fibromyalgia at rest and after moderate exercise, looking for subgroups and biomarkers.
diseno: Repeated-measures case-control study: 48 CFS patients (with or without FM), 18 with FM alone and 49 controls; 25-min exercise at 70% of maximum HR; qPCR of 13 genes in blood before and at 0.5, 8, 24 and 48 h.
hallazgos: In 71% of CFS patients, exercise increased for 48 h the transcription of sensory and adrenergic receptors and a cytokine, in correlation with fatigue and pain; the remaining 29% showed a decrease in the α-2A receptor, a subgroup with more orthostatic intolerance. Controls did not change and FM alone showed baseline increases of three genes.
conclusion: There are at least two CFS subgroups defined by gene response to exercise, and the post-exercise increase of four genes meets criteria as an objective biomarker that could guide treatment.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the structured abstract) are fully consistent around gene expression, exercise and sensory receptors; the keywords do not reflect the finding of subgroups or orthostatic intolerance.

tema: Pilot study exploring a possible genetic predisposition to ME/CFS through genome-scale SNP analysis.
diseno: Pilot genetic study in 383 ME/CFS participants genotyped by 23andMe; filtering of non-synonymous, nonsense, miRNA and near-splice-site SNPs; comparison with the Kaviar reference database, pathway overrepresentation analysis (ConsensusPathDB) and CADD scoring.
hallazgos: 5693 SNPs with at least 10% frequency and a minimum two-fold difference from the reference were identified, mostly in immune system, hormonal, metabolic and extracellular matrix organization pathways; 517 SNPs were among the 10% most deleterious substitutions according to CADD.
conclusion: The authors suggest a genetic predisposition in immune, hormonal and metabolic pathways, acknowledging that the analysis excludes non-coding regions and rare variants and that larger samples and more detailed statistical analyses are required.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on genetic susceptibility, SNPs and immune/metabolic dysfunction; the conclusions (taken from the discussion, with noise from acknowledgements and declarations) only provide limitations and future plans, qualifying the scope of the findings.

tema: Examines the interaction between polymorphisms and methylation of the COMT gene and its relationship to inflammatory markers and symptoms in CFS/fibromyalgia.
diseno: Case-control study with repeated-measures design: 28 CFS/FM patients and 26 controls assessed twice over 4 days; questionnaires, neurophysiological pain assessment, genotyping of rs4818, rs4633 and rs4680, methylation of MB-COMT and S-COMT promoters and expression of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-6 and TGF-β.
hallazgos: COMT haplotypes were associated with S-COMT promoter methylation, TGF-β expression and symptoms, but without disease specificity. Patients showed higher MB-COMT promoter methylation and lower IFN-γ expression.
conclusion: The prevalence of COMT polymorphisms and haplotypes is similar in patients and controls, whereas MB-COMT methylation and IFN-γ action could have clinical relevance; further investigation of methylation with repeated-measures designs is recommended.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent around COMT, methylation and epigenetics; the PDF conclusions are more explicit than the abstract in stating that the polymorphisms are not specific to CFS/FM, placing the focus on MB-COMT methylation.

tema: Genome-wide association study (GWAS) in ME/CFS with discovery and replication cohorts to identify risk loci.
diseno: GWAS with a Norwegian discovery cohort (N = 427), a Danish replication cohort (N = 460) and UK Biobank data (N = 2105); 2532 patients in the genomic analysis and 460 in the targeted analysis.
hallazgos: No locus reached genome-wide significance. The TPPP gene region showed the strongest association in the Norwegian cohort (rs115523291, P = 8.5 × 10−7) with the lead SNP not replicating, although other TPPP SNPs showed modest signals in UK Biobank and in the combined analysis (rs139264145; P = 0.00004).
conclusion: No risk loci were established despite this being the largest study to date, but several potential loci are identified; the authors call for cohorts of several thousand patients with strict phenotyping to analyse homogeneous subphenotypes.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion, with noise from acknowledgements and funding) are consistent; the title and conclusions speak of potential loci, whereas the abstract more clearly stresses the absence of genome-wide significance.

tema: Looks for genetic risk factors for severe long COVID and long COVID with fatigue predominance through combinatorial analysis, and their overlap with ME/CFS.
diseno: Combinatorial genetic analysis in two subpopulations of long COVID patients (severe and fatigue-predominant) from the Sano Genetics Long COVID GOLD cohort; comparison with previous ME/CFS genetic signatures and with other chronic diseases; pathway enrichment analysis.
hallazgos: 73 genes associated with at least one subpopulation were identified, 9 with prior association to acute COVID-19 and 14 differentially expressed in long COVID transcriptomics; the pathways aligned with neurological and cardiometabolic diseases. SNX9 genotypes, in interaction with KLF15 and RYR3, modulate the risk of severe long COVID; the severe subgroup was enriched in immune pathways and the fatigue one in metabolic pathways such as MAPK/JNK.
conclusion: Combinatorial analysis allows heterogeneous populations in complex non-monogenic diseases to be stratified, and the authors expect larger independent datasets to validate the findings and possible therapeutic options.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the combinatorial approach and the SNX9/KLF15 genes; the abstract appears truncated right at the part on overlap with ME/CFS, and the conclusions focus on the methodological value rather than on specific results about ME/CFS.

tema: Explores genotype-DNA methylation interactions in T lymphocytes associated with ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with epigenetic (~480,000 CpG loci) and genetic (~4.3 million SNPs) characterization in cohorts of ME/CFS patients and healthy controls; sample size not stated in the sources.
hallazgos: More than a hundred differentially methylated CpG loci were identified in T lymphocytes, nearly half clustered in regions of 500 bp or less, near genes of immune function and cellular metabolism. There were no direct large-effect associations between genotype and phenotype, but all differential methylation values correlated with genotypes of nearby SNPs.
conclusion: Genotype would appear to indirectly influence the methylation profiles associated with ME/CFS; the findings are considered preliminary and point to new research targets that require targeted validation and larger GWAS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are consistent on methylation, T lymphocytes and SNPs; the conclusions are more cautious, clarifying that the aim was not to identify biomarkers and that there were no large direct genetic effects.

tema: Evaluates Giardia-specific cellular immunity in people who developed CFS after a giardiasis outbreak compared with those who recovered.
diseno: Case-control study: 39 exposed patients evaluated five years after the outbreak (CFS n = 15, idiopathic chronic fatigue n = 5, fatigue from other causes n = 9, recovered n = 10), 20 exposed without fatigue and 10 unexposed controls; proliferation assays, T lymphocyte activation and cytokines in PBMC.
hallazgos: There were antigen-specific differences between exposed and unexposed, but not between the fatigue groups in CD4 activation, proliferation or cytokines. sCD40L was elevated in post-infectious CFS and other fatigued individuals, and correlated with the level of fatigue.
conclusion: T memory responses against Giardia are confirmed, with no differences in magnitude or quality with respect to post-giardiasis CFS, except for the increase in sCD40L in fatigued patients.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The PDF conclusions emphasize the negative result (absence of differences in T responses), whereas the abstract highlights the sCD40L finding more; the keywords include both.

tema: Documents a severity-based exercise intervention in a patient with severe ME/CFS and POTS.
diseno: Case report of a 44-year-old woman bedbound for 10-15 years; programme of seven exercises in a monthly class for 6 months, with active standing test, Fatigue Impact Score and activity records.
hallazgos: The fatigue impact score, activity levels and standing heart rate improved during the intervention and at follow-up.
conclusion: The intervention can have a positive effect in this patient; in a later group of six patients the effect was variable, so more research is needed on its autonomic action.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on POTS, autonomic dysfunction and exercise intervention; the PDF conclusions qualify the positive result by describing variable effects in an expanded group.

tema: Describes the haemodynamic changes during the 10-minute NASA Lean Test in ME/CFS according to disease duration.
diseno: Study with 150 ME/CFS patients (75 with less than 4 years of illness and 75 with more than 10) and 75 matched healthy controls; NASA Lean Test with blood pressure and heart rate every minute and symptom recording; ANOVA and regression.
hallazgos: At least 5 min were required to detect changes. The group with less than 4 years had higher heart rate, abnormally narrow pulse pressure and more OI symptoms, unrelated to age or medication.
conclusion: There is a subgroup of recent-onset ME/CFS with circulatory decompensation, probably due to insufficient ventricular filling; the NASA Lean Test is a simple tool for early diagnosis and for guiding OI treatment.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on haemodynamics, pulse pressure and OI; the venous pressure keyword reflects an inference, not a direct measurement.

tema: Reviews and proposes the hypothesis that herpesvirus infection of endothelial cells underlies the symptomatology of ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative review with proposal of a conceptual model on herpesvirus latency and reactivation in the endothelium.
hallazgos: Evidence is synthesized linking herpesviruses with persistent endothelial infection and its consequences: impaired regulation of blood flow and coagulation and cognitive impairment, symptoms compatible with ME/CFS and long COVID.
conclusion: Herpesvirus-induced endothelial maladaptation could partly explain the chronicity and multisystem nature of ME/CFS; the prevalence and burden of endothelial infection in patients needs to be investigated.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions qualify that endothelial infection would not explain all the pathology, since infection of immune and nerve cells would also contribute.

tema: Reanalyses herpesvirus serology to check whether it distinguishes subgroups of ME/CFS patients according to the trigger of the disease.
diseno: Reanalysis of serological data (7 herpesvirus antigens) from the UK ME/CFS Biobank: S0 (n = 42, unknown trigger), S1 (n = 43, non-infectious), S2 (n = 93, unconfirmed infectious), S3 (n = 48, confirmed infectious) and 99 healthy controls; sensitivity analysis with variable cut-off points and correction for multiple testing.
hallazgos: S1 showed a negative association with seropositivity to EBV (VCA, EBNA1) and varicella-zoster virus, not significant after correction. S3 had lower cytomegalovirus seroprevalence for all cut-off points after Benjamini-Hochberg, but not with Benjamini-Yekutieli.
conclusion: Herpesvirus serology could distinguish subgroups according to the trigger, although the finding may be affected by the problem of multiple comparisons.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The conclusions text is only contributions and funding, so it provides no information; the abstract's conclusion is already cautious.

tema: Empirically identifies CFS subgroups from the baseline data of the PACE trial.
diseno: Latent class analysis with 26 variables in 541 of the 640 PACE trial participants, after variable reduction with PCA and clinical judgement.
hallazgos: Five subgroups: 'core' (33%), mood disorders (21%), features of other functional somatic syndromes (21%), many symptoms (14%) and 'avoidant-inactive' (11%); differences in fatigue and disability gave some validation.
conclusion: CFS is heterogeneous; the subgroups could guide aetiological research and personalized treatments (e.g., CBT for the avoidant-inactive subgroup).
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add subgroup-specific treatment hypotheses not present in the abstract.

tema: Computational analysis investigating why circulating miRNAs altered in ME/CFS differ between studies and whether they converge on common gene targets.
diseno: Computational study of predicted gene targets of circulating miRNAs described in the literature, with analysis of functional interactions, directional pathway information and network centrality, plus literature review on herpesviruses; no own patient sample.
hallazgos: The aberrant miRNAs, although different between studies, mainly target the same set of genes (p ≈ 0.0018), highly functionally related (p ≲ 0.0001). The pathways point to alterations in exercise hyperaemia, angiogenic adaptation to hypoxia, antioxidant defences, TGF-β signalling and mitochondrial fission; 8 of the 10 most central miRNAs are known to be induced by herpesviruses.
conclusion: Circulating miRNAs would have an appreciable and possibly central role in the aetiology of ME/CFS, which justifies experimental research, for example exposing cell cultures to patient serum.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on miRNAs, exercise hyperaemia, antioxidant defences and TGF-β; the conclusions (from the discussion, with noise from supplementary material and contributions) add limitations of the databases (oncological bias of miRTarBase) and call for experimental validation.

tema: Studies in a rat model of chronic fatigue the alterations in thermoregulatory homeostasis.
diseno: Experimental study in rats with fatigue loading by intermittent water immersion; measurement of temperature and heat dissipation through the tail with infrared thermography evaluated double-blind. The available abstract is only the header of the manuscript; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Adaptive changes in thermoregulatory function were observed with the progression of fatigue, with altered heat dissipation through the tail and signs compatible with low-grade fever.
conclusion: The homeostatic thermoregulatory system could be altered by prolonged fatigue loading, suggesting that its functional disruption underlies the chronification of fatigue, in line with the abnormal thermosensation of CFS patients.
triangulacion: The abstract lacks scientific content (it is opening text), so triangulation is based on keywords and discussion, which are consistent (thermoregulation, rat model, low-grade fever). The discussion includes noise from contributions and funding.

tema: Determines the risk of CFS after the diagnosis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection (MTI).
diseno: Population-based retrospective cohort (Taiwan National Health Insurance database): 7666 patients ≥20 years with MTI diagnosed in 2000-2011 and 30,663 without MTI; Cox proportional hazards regression.
hallazgos: The incidence of CFS was 3.69 versus 3.04 per 1000 person-years (adjusted HR 1.23; 95% CI 1.03-1.47). The risk was higher in men (HR 1.27) and in those ≥65 years (HR 2.50).
conclusion: MTI is associated with an elevated risk of subsequent CFS; the authors consider the pilot finding useful for identifying high-risk individuals and call for studying the mechanisms.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on tuberculosis, risk factors, age and sex. The PDF conclusions describe the finding as 'pilot' and do not address the immunological effects announced by the title.

tema: Analyses the risk of developing CFS in patients with peptic ulcer disease (PUD) compared with patients without it.
diseno: National retrospective cohort from Taiwan's Longitudinal Health Insurance Database 2000; comparison of incidences with adjustment for age, sex and comorbidities. Sample size not stated in the abstract.
hallazgos: The incidence of CFS was higher in the PUD cohort (HR 2.01; 95% CI 1.75-2.30, unchanged after adjustment), with a significant relative risk in both sexes and an incidence that increased with age.
conclusion: There is an increased risk of CFS after PUD, especially in women and older people; PUD prevention could be relevant for public health, although the findings do not contribute to the diagnosis of CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The keywords mention Helicobacter pylori, which the abstract only presents as a frequent cause of PUD without analysing it directly; the conclusions are more cautious in acknowledging that they do not contribute to diagnosis.

tema: Investigates associations of HLA alleles with ME/CFS as an indication of autoimmune mechanisms.
diseno: Case-control study: high-resolution HLA genotyping (-A, -B, -C, -DRB1, -DQB1, -DPB1) by next-generation sequencing in 426 Norwegian patients (Canadian criteria) versus 4511 ethnically matched healthy controls; clinical questionnaires.
hallazgos: Two independent associations were found: HLA-C*07:04 (OR 2.1 [95% CI 1.4–3.1]) and HLA-DQB1*03:03 (OR 1.5 [95% CI 1.1–2.0]), carried by 7.7% and 12.7% of patients. 19.2% of patients versus 12.2% of controls carried one or both alleles (OR 1.7; pnc = 0.00003).
conclusion: The new HLA associations point to the involvement of the immune system in the pathogenesis of ME/CFS, a complex and potentially heterogeneous disease.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on HLA, autoimmunity and genetic susceptibility; the extracted conclusions text actually corresponds to statistical methods and provides no conclusions, so triangulation relies only on the keywords and abstract.

tema: Reflection on the professional ethics of psychotherapy as support, not treatment, in ME/CFS and medically unexplained symptoms.
diseno: Reflective article based on recent empirical literature and on four ethical principles from codes of practice.
hallazgos: Survey data and qualitative research suggest that psychotherapeutic practice sometimes fails to meet the ethical standards of respect, competence, responsibility and integrity.
conclusion: They recommend humility and reflective practice, integrating patient experience into training, feedback systems, access to clinical notes and co-production of research with patients.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions (from the discussion) detail the practical proposals and emphasize the marginalization of these patients.
